e: Earth slides right between the Sun and the Moon, casting its own shadow onto the Moon.

q: What particles inside the center of an atom have no electrical charge at all?
e: Neutrons are totally neutral, keeping peaceful company with protons inside the nucleus.

q: Why do wheels and balls need to be round instead of square to roll smoothly?
a: Round shapes have no weight at all
Every point on the edge is the same distance from the center
Squares create less friction with the ground
Circles naturally generate their own wind power
e: Because every side is evenly curved, round objects roll smoothly without bumping up and down.

q: About how long does it take for sunlight to travel from the Sun to Earth?
e: Even though light is blazing fast, the Sun is ninety-three million miles away, taking eight minutes to visit!

q: What happens to water inside a coal or natural gas power plant to spin the turbines?
e: Boiling water makes high-pressure steam that blows like a whistling kettle to spin the heavy turbines.

q: Which simple machine turns the wheels when you push down on bicycle pedals?
e: Pedals turn a center rod called an axle, which spins the chain and wheels!

q: How does a floating raindrop help create the colors of a rainbow?
a: It bends and separates white light
It paints the sky with liquid colors
It freezes light into ice crystals
It absorbs all colors except blue
e: Each raindrop acts like a tiny glass prism, splitting ordinary sunlight into every color hidden inside.

q: Which European city suffered a huge fire in 1666 that started in a bakery?
e: The Great Fire of London started in a baker's oven on Pudding Lane and spread across the city.

q: Why does a mouse make a higher sound than a lion?
e: Tiny vocal cords can flutter back and forth rapidly, creating that adorable, high-pitched squeak.

q: Which gas makes up the greatest amount of matter inside the burning Sun?
e: Hydrogen is the Sun's favorite fuel, making up about three-quarters of this giant glowing ball.

q: What happens to an inflated rubber balloon if you leave it in a cold freezer?
a: It pops because cold air expands
It floats upward to the ceiling
It shrinks because cold air takes up less space
e: Cold air huddles close together, taking up less room and making the balloon look squished.

q: What happens to a comet each time it loops closely around the hot Sun?
a: It loses some of its ice and dust
It turns completely into solid gold
It freezes harder and doubles in size
It stops moving and stays there forever
e: Every hot trip past the Sun bakes away a little more of the comet's icy body.

q: What happens when a child covers all the finger holes on a recorder?
e: Covering every hole makes the air column inside as long as possible, dropping the pitch down low.

q: Why does a car need a longer distance to stop on a wet road?
a: Water creates less friction between tires and road
e: Water makes the road slippery, giving the tires less grip to slow the car down quickly.

q: What kind of invisible rays from the Sun can cause painful sunburns on skin?
e: Ultraviolet rays carry extra energy that can scorch bare skin, which is why sunscreen is your best friend.

q: What is the deepest known trench in the oceans of planet Earth?
e: The Mariana Trench plunges nearly seven miles straight down into total ocean darkness.

q: How long does reflected moonlight take to travel across space to reach Earth?
e: Since the Moon is our closest neighbor in space, light hops over to us in just over a second!

q: Which bicycle gear makes it easiest for your legs to pedal up a hill?
e: Low gears let your feet spin freely with little strain, making big steep hills feel like a breeze!

q: What happens if an astronaut cries tears while floating inside a space station?
a: Tears instantly spray outward like tiny water fountains
Tears stick together and form a liquid ball over the eye
Tears freeze into tiny ice crystals on their cheeks
Tears run down their face faster than on Earth
e: Without gravity to pull tears down your cheek, they cling together and form a big watery blob.

q: What is the special liquid flowing through refrigerator pipes called?
e: Refrigerant is a clever fluid that easily switches between liquid and gas to carry heat away.

q: In which European country was the first practical telescope invented during the early 1600s?
e: Dutch lens maker Hans Lippershey lined up two glasses in 1608, creating the very first working telescope.

q: What kind of station sits between high-voltage power lines and your local neighborhood streets?
e: Substations are fenced-in yards where big transformers tame super-strong electricity before sending it down local streets.

q: Why was the 'QWERTY' letter layout originally created for mechanical typewriters?
a: To keep metal typing bars from jamming
e: Spacing out commonly paired letters stopped old mechanical typewriter arms from clashing and getting stuck together.

q: What can you adjust on a home thermostat in winter to save energy when sleeping?
a: Turn the temperature all the way up
Turn the temperature down a few degrees
e: Snuggling under warm blankets lets your heater rest at a lower setting all night.

q: Why does a raw egg float in salty water but sink in fresh tap water?
a: Salt makes the egg much lighter
Salty water is denser and pushes it up
Salt creates tiny air pockets around the egg
Fresh water pulls the egg down with magnets
e: Adding salt packs more stuff into the water, giving it extra muscle to lift the egg.

q: What are the dark, cooler patches that sometimes appear on the Sun's bright surface?
e: Sunspots look dark only because they are slightly cooler than the fiery surface around them.

q: What does a safety fuse do when too much electricity flows through it?
a: It adds extra power to the wires
It melts to break the circuit safely
It turns electricity into ice water
It plays a loud horn sound
e: A fuse heroically melts itself to cut off the dangerous power and prevent fires!

q: Which famous passenger airplane could fly faster than sound across the Atlantic Ocean?
e: The Concorde was so speedy that passengers could fly from London to New York in just over three hours!

q: In which of these materials does sound travel the fastest?
e: In solid metal, atoms are packed super tightly, so vibrations can bounce across them instantly.

q: What is the name of NASA's new space program designed to land astronauts on the Moon again?
e: The Artemis program is preparing to send astronauts, including the first woman, back to explore the Moon.

q: Why do different cities around the world have different clock times?
a: Because Earth is round and spins
Because every city chooses random hours
Because the Moon controls the clocks
Because rivers flow at different speeds
e: Since Earth spins, morning arrives in some cities while others are fast asleep.

q: What does the numbered dial on the front of a toaster control?
a: How long the heat stays on
e: Higher numbers keep the heating wires cooking longer, turning your bread from golden to extra crispy!

q: Why does touching a metal spoon feel colder than touching a wooden board at room temperature?
a: Wood is always naturally warmer than the room
Metal produces its own freezing frost
Metal pulls heat away from your fingers much faster
Wood reflects all room temperature away
e: Metal is a speedy conductor that steals heat from your warm finger, making it feel extra chilly.

q: Why must space rockets travel so fast to stay in orbit around Earth?
a: To escape the heat of the Sun
To push through thick outer space
To keep their rocket engines running
To keep from falling back to Earth
e: Rockets must speed sideways at seventeen thousand miles per hour to constantly miss falling into the planet.

q: Why do solid ice cubes float on top of liquid water?
a: Ice is lighter and less dense than water
Ice attracts air from the room
e: Because freezing water spreads out, ice is actually lighter than the liquid it floats in!

q: What old invention used wind power centuries ago to grind wheat into flour?
e: Long before electricity, clever farmers let spinning windmill sails crush grain into yummy flour.

q: What is the name of an electrical circuit with an accidental gap?
e: If the loop opens up anywhere, the path breaks and electricity comes to a sudden stop.

q: How does the Sun provide the energy needed to create rain clouds?
e: Warm sunshine heats puddles and seas, turning water into floating vapor that forms fluffy clouds.

q: What tiny wedge inside a coat zipper joins or separates the metal teeth?
e: The zipper slide has a wedge inside that pushes teeth together or splits them apart.

q: Where does a computer keep your photos and saved games after you turn it off?
e: Storage drives hold onto your files safely for years, even when the power is completely turned off.

q: A lunar eclipse can occur only during what phase of the moon?
e: Earth hides the sun's light by stepping right between them, casting its cozy shadow only when the moon is completely full.

q: What is the location of the moon at the new moon stage?
a: Between the earth and the sun
On the opposite side of the earth from the sun
On the opposite side of the sun from the earth
To the side of a line between the earth and the sun
e: During a new moon, the moon tiptoes right between Earth and the sun, turning its bright, shiny face away to play hide-and-seek.

q: A total solar eclipse can occur only during what phase of the moon?
e: The moon must step right between Earth and the sun, hiding its bright face as a shadowy new moon.

q: Approximately what percentage of water on Earth is fresh water?
e: Earth is a giant blue puddle, but only three percent is sweet fresh water we can actually drink.
